failure_context.from_triage: RT-Thread RV32D smoke simulation bus fault
failure_context.failure_class: misaligned floating-point context restore and recursive trap
failure_context.suspected_area: initial thread stack construction and RV32D context save/restore

signals_traced.reason: identify the first failing FLD in the initial thread restore path
confirm the effective address and alignment of RV32D context transfers
trace the initial alignment exception and recursive trap sequence

observations: The initial thread restore executes fld ft0,0(sp) with sp equal to 0x1000138c, which is only four-byte aligned.
The FLD raises mcause=4 (load address misaligned).
The exception entry then attempts FSD context saves on the same misaligned stack and raises mcause=6 (store address misaligned), recursively entering the trap path.
Repeated recursive context saves eventually move outside the DATA memory region and appear at the SoC level as a bus fault.

root_cause.description: The RT-Thread initial stack frame was aligned to four bytes, but the RV32D context restore/save code uses FLD/FSD and therefore requires eight-byte alignment; the RISC-V ABI baseline uses sixteen-byte stack alignment.
root_cause.evidence: First failing FLD address 0x1000138c, followed by mcause=4 and recursive FSD mcause=6 traps.

fix_recommendation.description: Align the initial RT-Thread stack pointer down to 16 bytes before constructing the RV32IMFD context frame.
